answers.answer: BAM is a compressed binary encoding of exactly the same information

question: Why must a BAM file be sorted by position before it can be indexed?

answers.answer: The index lets tools jump straight to a genomic region, which only works if records are ordered by position
samtools cannot read unsorted files at all
answers.feedback: It can — it just cannot index them.

question: The number of lines in the SAM file does not match the number of lines in the FASTQ file. Why not?

answers.answer: FASTQ uses four lines per read, while SAM uses one line per alignment — plus header lines and any supplementary alignments
bwa discarded most of the reads
answers.feedback: Unmapped reads are still written out.

answers.answer: SAM stores only one mate of each pair
